sentences.text:
Balagani Venkata Prasad Prasad, vs The State Of Andhra
Pradesh, on 16 October, 2019

Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.6132 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A1 & A3 to A9 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.86 of 2019 of Medarametla Police Station, Prakasam District, which was registered against them for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 328, 420, 468, 466, 471, 474, 120-B r/w.Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006).

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 23.08.2019 at about 16:00 hours, the complainant along with his staff on credible information raided the Nikhita Tobacco godowns at Ravinuthala Road, Medarametla Village of Korisapadu Mandal, seized the banned products under a cover of mediators report and arrested the accused.

Later, he registered the mediators report as a case in Crime No.86 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.
3.

Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 & batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto filed on the report of the Circle Inspector of Police of Medarametla Police Station.

Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore,
the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners/A1 & A3 to A9 under Sections 188, 272, 328,
420, 468, 466, 471, 474, 120-B r/w.Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
